title: Prepare for catastrophe
intro: Most experts do not think disaster is certain. But many leading researchers think the risk is real enough to prepare for, the same way we prepare for pandemics and nuclear war.

risk_categories.name: Misuse
risk_categories.simple: A person or group uses AI on purpose to do harm, like scams, cyber attacks or help with weapons.
examples: AI voice clones used to trick families into sending money
AI used to find and exploit software bugs
AI giving step by step help for dangerous chemistry or biology

evidence.text: Misuse occurs when a human deliberately uses an AI system for harmful purposes.
General-purpose AI systems can be misused for fraud and cybercrime, manipulation of users, and potentially harmful applications in biological and chemical domains.

risk_categories.name: Misalignment
risk_categories.simple: The AI ends up wanting something different from what we meant, and may hide it from us.
examples: Narrow bad training spreading into broad bad behavior

evidence.text: If trained like today's most capable models, AGIs could learn to act deceptively to receive higher reward, learn misaligned internally-represented goals which generalize beyond their fine-tuning distributions, and pursue those goals using power-seeking strategies.
We present a demonstration of a large language model engaging in alignment faking

risk_categories.name: Loss of control
risk_categories.simple: AI systems become so capable and independent that humans can no longer correct them or switch them off.
examples: Models sabotaging a shutdown script in tests
Hundreds of AI agents coordinating a hack without telling humans
AI that trains its own successor with no human in the loop

evidence.text: These risks range from the further entrenchment of existing inequalities, to manipulation and misinformation, to the loss of control of autonomous AI systems potentially resulting in human extinction.
We have no idea whether we can stay in control.
sometimes actively subvert a shutdown mechanism in their environment to complete that task

risk_categories.name: Concentration of power
risk_categories.simple: A small group, a company or one leader uses advanced AI to grab and keep power over everyone else.
examples: A few companies controlling the most powerful systems

evidence.text: An AI-enabled coup could be staged by a very small group, or just a single person, and could occur even in established democracies.
Alongside the benefits, AI will also bring dangers, like powerful autonomous weapons, or new ways for the few to oppress the many.

risk_categories.name: Biological risk
risk_categories.simple: AI could help someone make or improve a dangerous germ or toxin.
examples: Lab instructions and troubleshooting from chatbots
Labs restricting biology abilities in their strongest models

evidence.text: Advances in AI’s scientific capabilities have heightened concerns about misuse in biological weapons development.
In the near future AI may be used to create terrible new viruses and horrendous lethal weapons that decide by themselves who to kill or maim.

risk_categories.name: Cyber risk
risk_categories.simple: AI can find and use security holes faster than people can fix them, and AI agents can attack on their own.
examples: Claude Mythos Preview held back for its hacking skill

evidence.text: Mythos Preview’s success on one cyber range indicates that it is at least capable of autonomously attacking small, weakly defended and vulnerable enterprise systems where access to a network has been gained.
We consider this incident a 'warning shot' for us and for the world

risk_categories.name: Racing and accidents
risk_categories.simple: Companies and countries rush to stay ahead, so they cut safety corners and mistakes slip through.
examples: Safety teams losing out to product launches
Labs saying they cannot pause alone while rivals keep going

evidence.text: safety culture and processes have taken a backseat to shiny products.
AI race, in which competitive environments compel actors to deploy unsafe AIs or cede control to AIs

proposals.name: Responsible scaling policies (RSPs)
proposals.simple: If-then rules: if a model reaches a dangerous ability level, then the lab must add stronger safeguards or stop.

evidence.text: Responsible Scaling Policy

proposals.limits: These are voluntary, and companies can rewrite them.

proposals.name: Frontier safety frameworks
proposals.who: Google DeepMind, OpenAI and others; promised at the 2024 Seoul summit
proposals.simple: Labs list 'critical capability levels' and test new models to see if they cross them.

evidence.text: Evaluating our frontier models periodically to detect when they reach these Critical Capability Levels.
In the extreme, organisations commit not to develop or deploy a model or system at all, if mitigations cannot be applied to keep risks below the thresholds.

proposals.limits: Labs write and grade their own frameworks.

proposals.name: Dangerous capability evaluations
proposals.who: METR, Apollo Research, UK AI Security Institute, US CAISI, IndiaAI Safety Institute
proposals.simple: Independent testers try to make models do dangerous things before and after release, so surprises are caught early.

evidence.text: Yeah, so basically, the basic mission is: have the world not be taken by surprise by dangerous AI stuff happening.

proposals.limits: Models may notice they are being tested and behave differently.

proposals.name: AI control
proposals.who: Redwood Research and lab safety teams
proposals.simple: Design monitoring and limits so that even a scheming AI cannot cause a disaster.

evidence.text: Labs should make sure that powerful models can't cause unacceptably bad outcomes even if the AIs try to.

proposals.limits: May stop working once AI is far smarter than its monitors.

proposals.name: Kill switches and shutdown ability
proposals.who: Proposed in laws like California SB 1047; tested by Palisade Research
proposals.simple: Developers must be able to fully shut down a model they control.

evidence.text: kill switch
sometimes actively subvert a shutdown mechanism in their environment

proposals.limits: Tests show some models already try to avoid shutdown, and copies that escape cannot be switched off.

proposals.name: Compute governance
proposals.who: Researchers at GovAI, Epoch AI and governments
proposals.simple: Track and control the chips and data centers used to train the biggest models, since compute is easy to see and count.

evidence.text: Relative to other key inputs to AI (data and algorithms), AI-relevant compute is a particularly effective point of intervention: it is detectable, excludable, and quantifiable, and is produced via an extremely concentrated supply chain.

proposals.limits: Smarter algorithms can need less compute over time.

proposals.name: Interpretability
proposals.simple: Look inside models to see what they are really thinking before they get too powerful.

evidence.text: We therefore must move fast if we want interpretability to mature in time to matter.

proposals.limits: The science is young and models are growing faster than our tools.

proposals.name: Whistleblower protection
proposals.who: Current and former lab employees (A Right to Warn)
proposals.simple: Let insiders warn the public and regulators about serious risks without losing their jobs or money.

evidence.text: These risks range from the further entrenchment of existing inequalities

proposals.limits: Needs real laws, not just company promises.

proposals.name: Prohibit superintelligence
proposals.who: FLI Statement on Superintelligence, ControlAI, the 2026 Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act
proposals.simple: Do not build AI smarter than all humans until there is scientific agreement it can be done safely and the public agrees.

evidence.text: We call for a prohibition on the development of superintelligence, not lifted before there is broad scientific consensus that it will be done safely and controllably, and strong public buy-in.

proposals.limits: Needs agreement between rival countries and a way to check it.

proposals.name: Shared international science
proposals.who: International AI Safety Report (30+ countries), AI summits from Bletchley to New Delhi
proposals.simple: Countries agree on the facts about AI risk first, so they can act together.

evidence.text: There is potential for serious, even catastrophic, harm, either deliberate or unintentional, stemming from the most significant capabilities of these AI models.

proposals.limits: Reports do not make binding rules.

proposals.name: India's AI governance guidelines
proposals.simple: India's principle-based framework sets up an AI Governance Group, an expert committee and the IndiaAI Safety Institute.

evidence.text: The guidelines recommends establishment of new national institutions including the AI Governance Group, Technology & Policy Expert Committee, and AI Safety Institute.

proposals.name: Defensive acceleration (d/acc)
proposals.simple: Speed up technology that protects people, like better cyber defense and biosecurity, faster than technology that attacks.

evidence.text: AI is fundamentally different from other tech, and it is worth being uniquely careful

what_you_can_do.title: Take a free intro course
steps: Start BlueDot's self-paced Future of AI course
Then try AGI Strategy, Technical AI Safety or Frontier AI Governance

what_you_can_do.title: Read one clear explainer a week
steps: Browse plain answers on AISafety.info
Read MIRI's The Problem and, for balance, AI as Normal Technology

what_you_can_do.title: Find your place on the field map
steps: Use AISafety.com to find courses, events, communities and jobs near you

what_you_can_do.title: Plan a career in AI safety
steps: Read the 80,000 Hours AI safety research career review
Check the 80,000 Hours job board for roles

what_you_can_do.title: Build research skills
steps: Work through ARENA's exercises
Apply to SPAR, ERA or MATS when you are ready

what_you_can_do.title: Ship small safety projects
steps: Pick an open problem from a mechanistic interpretability guide
Write it up on GitHub or LessWrong and share it

what_you_can_do.title: Tell your representatives you care
steps: Email or call your lawmakers about AI risk
Sign a public statement you agree with

what_you_can_do.title: Join a community
steps: Join a volunteer group, onboarding call or local meetup
Talk about AI risk calmly with friends and family

what_you_can_do.title: Protect your family from AI scams
steps: Agree a secret word or phrase with your family
Look for small glitches in videos and voices
Never send money just because a voice sounds familiar

evidence.text: Create a secret word or phrase with your family to verify their identity.

what_you_can_do.title: Lock down your accounts
steps: Turn on 2-step verification
Install software and app updates quickly
Use strong, separate passwords

evidence.text: Turn on 2-step verification (2SV)

what_you_can_do.title: Keep a basic emergency kit
steps: Store water, food, medicine, a torch and a battery radio
Keep copies of important documents
This helps in any disaster, including cyber attacks on power or banks

evidence.text: A disaster supplies kit is a collection of basic items your household may need in the event of an emergency.

what_you_can_do.title: Stay calm and keep acting
steps: Take the risk seriously without panic
Spend time offline with real people
Small steady actions beat fear

note: Quotes in evidence are exact text checked against the source page on 2026-10-29. Personal resilience tips are general safety advice from government sources, not AI-specific guarantees.
